# Jubilees Chapter 22 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 22:4 — "fat things of the earth" vs. "good things of the earth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all the fat-things of the earth" | Literal Ge'ez shebeḥat = fat/rich things |
| LOGOS | "all the fat things of the earth" | Same — preserves the idiom |
| PNEUMA | "filled the earth with good things" | Dynamic, loses the specific "fat" idiom |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET. "Fat things" is the standard biblical idiom for earth's rich produce (cf. Gen 27:28, 39); PNEUMA's "good things" is acceptable but loses the specific flavor of the Ge'ez.

---

## 22:9 — "Lord and Light of the nations"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you are the Lord and Light of the nations" | Literal — unusual title applied to Jacob |
| LOGOS | "you are the Lord and Light of the nations" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "you are the light and the lord of the nations" | Inverts the order |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS. "Lord and Light" is the Ge'ez order and should be preserved. PNEUMA's inversion ("light and the lord") is a minor deviation but the original sequence "Lord and Light" should be retained as it appears in the manuscript tradition.

---

## 22:11 — "do not eat with them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "associate not with the nations, and eat not with them" | Literal double prohibition |
| LOGOS | "Do not associate with the nations, and do not eat with them" | Same, formal |
| PNEUMA | "Don't mix with the nations. Don't sit at their tables." | Paraphrase — "tables" not in text |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The prohibition on table fellowship (commensality) is a serious halakhic boundary in Jubilees; LOGOS states it plainly. PNEUMA's "tables" is an interpretation. EMET's archaic negatives are fine but LOGOS is cleaner.

---

## 22:15 — Canaan's sin and Ham's sin: causal relationship

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "for when Ham sinned, Canaan also sinned" | Literal — treats Canaan as co-sinner with Ham |
| LOGOS | "For when Ham sinned, Canaan also sinned" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Ham sinned, and Canaan sinned with him" | Slight different emphasis |

**SOPHIA:** All three agree substantively. Adopted LOGOS. The theological point — that Canaan participated in the sin, not just inherited the curse — is Jubilees' distinctive reading of the Noah episode. All translators preserve this.

---

## 22:23 — "double cave" designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in the double-cave" | Hyphenated literal |
| LOGOS | "in the double cave" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "in the cave at Machpelah" | Substitutes proper name |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Double cave" is the Ge'ez's rendering of me'arat hamakhpelah — it should be preserved as the text's own designation. PNEUMA's "Machpelah" is clarifying but inserts a Hebrew proper name not present in the Ge'ez at this point.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
